R001.fact: If a complex vector space has finite dimension n and an indexed family consists of n linearly independent vectors, that family is a basis.

grounds.reason: V has finite complex dimension λ+1.
The finite index set I has n elements and n>0.
Before the basis conclusion, the polynomial isolation argument proves linear independence of the e_i.

R001.justification: Choose a basis of n vectors, whose existence is part of finite dimension n, and express the given family as the columns of an n by n complex matrix. Independence says the homogeneous system has only the zero solution. Finite Gaussian elimination therefore has a pivot in every column and, since the matrix is square, every row. Thus every coordinate vector is a linear combination of the columns. The family spans and is independent, hence is a basis.

R001.fact: For integers m≥r≥0, m(m−1)⋯(m−r+1)/r!=binom(m,r) is an integer, with value 1 for r=0. Consequently the rising product (a+1)⋯(a+r)/r!=binom(a+r,r) is an integer for integers a,r≥0.

grounds.reason: λ is a nonnegative integer.
i∈I means i is an integer with 0≤i≤λ.
r is an arbitrary natural number in S004.
For the x branch take a=λ−i≥0; for the y branch take a=i≥0. The respective products are exactly these rising products.

R001.justification: On an m-element set the number of ordered r-tuples of distinct elements is m(m−1)⋯(m−r+1). Partition these tuples by their underlying r-element subset. Every class has r! elements, one for each ordering, so the quotient is the number of r-element subsets, the binomial coefficient. The empty tuple gives the r=0 case. Reversing the factors with m=a+r gives the rising-product identity.

R002.fact: An integer basis of M which is also a complex basis of the finite-dimensional V can be reindexed by I when |I|=dim_C V=n.

grounds.reason: H004 supplies the simultaneous lattice and complex basis.
N001 supplies finite dimension n and |I|=n.

R002.justification: Any basis of an n-dimensional vector space has n elements: the finite exchange argument bounds an independent family by the size of a spanning family, applied in both directions to two bases. A bijection between its index set and I then reindexes both basis properties without changing any vector.

R002.fact: For a Z-linear endomorphism T of M, scalar extension to any commutative Z-algebra S is the S-linear endomorphism of S⊗_Z M determined by s⊗m↦s⊗T(m). For S=R and complex-linear T on V restricting to M, this extension intertwines μ with T. An injective R-linear map carrying an R-basis to a complex basis identifies its image as a free R-module of that rank spanning V.

grounds.reason: H004 supplies preservation of M by every divided power.
H002 supplies h=xy−yx, so h also preserves M after x=X_1 and y=Y_1.
R is viewed inside C.
μ(r⊗m)=rm.
V_K=M⊗_Z K; K is a commutative Z-algebra as a field.
M001 has provided the tensor basis, whose images are the complex basis chosen from F001.

R002.justification: The displayed pure-tensor formula respects additivity and integer balancing because T is Z-linear; hence it descends to the tensor product. Equality with Tμ holds on pure tensors and therefore on their finite sums. Every kernel vector has a finite expansion in the tensor basis; its images give a complex-linear relation, so all R-coefficients vanish since R embeds in C. The images of the basis then freely generate the image and span V over C. The same tensor construction with M⊗_Z K gives the asserted K-linear induced operators.

R002.fact: If p is prime and 0≤j≤λ<p, then p does not divide binom(λ,j), and binom(λ,j) is a unit of R=Z_(p).

grounds.reason: p is prime and 0≤λ<p.
j∈I means 0≤j≤λ.
A rational with denominator prime to p lies in R.

R002.justification: Every positive factor in λ! lies strictly between 0 and p. Reduction modulo p is in the field Z/pZ, so the product of these nonzero residues is nonzero; the empty product for λ=0 is 1. The integer identity λ!=binom(λ,j)j!(λ−j)! then rules out p dividing binom(λ,j). Its rational reciprocal belongs to R and multiplies it to 1.

R003.fact: If g_1,...,g_m generate J as an R-module and R⊂Q, then g_1,...,g_m span QJ=span_Q J over Q. In particular QJ has finite dimension.

grounds.reason: F001 proves finite generation of J.
R is the specified subring of Q.
QJ is the rational span of J.

R003.justification: Every element of J is an R-linear combination of the generators, hence a rational combination. Substituting into a finite rational combination proves the spanning assertion. Successively discard each generator lying in the span of its predecessors; the retained finite list is independent and still spans, hence is a finite basis.

R003.fact: For an R-linear map g:U→W and a commutative R-algebra Q, the balanced rule q⊗u↦q⊗g(u) defines a Q-linear map Q⊗_R U→Q⊗_R W. Such tensor products are generated over Q by pure tensors, so two Q-linear maps agreeing on pure tensors agree everywhere.

grounds.reason: F001 supplies R-linear coordinate and insertion maps with both composite identities.
S004 uses these maps between M_R and J and takes finite sums indexed by I.
R⊂Q supplies the algebra structure.
I is finite.

R003.justification: The proposed rule is additive in each factor and respects (qa)⊗u=q⊗(au) because g(au)=ag(u); the tensor universal property supplies the map. A tensor product is constructed from finite sums of pure tensors modulo the bilinearity and balancing relations. Consequently checking each composite on pure tensors and extending by linearity proves S004's inverse identities.

R003.fact: A vector space over Q with a finite spanning set has a finite basis; the cardinality of any finite basis is its dimension, and a linear isomorphism preserves that dimension. Moreover an injective Q-linear map Q^a→Q^b forces a≤b, so Q satisfies the strong rank condition required by M003.

grounds.reason: F002 establishes finite-dimensional QJ.
F003 identifies T_Q with QJ and establishes its finite dimension.
F004 is a Q-linear isomorphism from A_Q to (T_Q)^I.
N002 supplies a free R-module of rank n.
M001 supplies the scalar-extended Q-basis.

R003.justification: Pruning a finite spanning list gives a basis. Gaussian elimination over a field shows that an independent list in the span of b vectors has at most b members: each pivot uses a distinct one of the b rows. Applying this in both directions to finite bases proves equality of their sizes. An isomorphism carries a basis to a basis. Under an injection Q^a→Q^b, the images of the a standard basis vectors are independent, so elimination yields a≤b. Finite bases also directly establish freeness and finite generation used in M003.

R004.fact: If L is a one-dimensional Q-subspace of C, 0 != a belongs to L, and a nonzero finitely generated R-submodule J of L is given, then J has a finite nonempty generating list q_1 a,...,q_k a with each q_j a nonzero and each q_j in Q\{0}.

grounds.reason: J is nonzero and finitely generated and dim_Q QJ=1.
QJ is the rational span of J, so J is contained in QJ.
a is chosen nonzero in J.

R004.justification: A nonzero vector in a one-dimensional vector space spans it: relative to any one-element basis, its coefficient is nonzero and can be inverted. Express each member of a finite generating list in this basis a. Removing zero members preserves the generated submodule and cannot remove all members since J is nonzero. The surviving rational coefficients are nonzero.

R004.fact: For a positive prime integer p and any nonzero rational q, there are nu in Z and u in Q with q=p^nu u and both u and u^(-1) in Z_(p). A finite nonempty list of such integer exponents has an attained minimum.

grounds.reason: p is prime, hence p>=2.
F001 gives finitely many nonzero rational coefficients with positive list length.
R consists of rational fractions whose denominator is not divisible by p.

R004.justification: Write q=A/B with nonzero integers A,B. For each nonzero integer m, the exponents e>=0 for which p^e divides m form a nonempty finite set: divisibility implies p^e<=|m| and p>=2 bounds e. Choose its largest exponent. Thus A=p^alpha A' and B=p^beta B', with neither A' nor B' divisible by p. Set nu=alpha-beta and u=A'/B'. Both u and its reciprocal have allowed denominators in R, so u is an R-unit. Negative nu causes no problem in Q. Comparing finitely many integer entries recursively yields an entry realizing their minimum. This is the factorization and minimum construction already used in S002.

R004.fact: If R is a subring of C, (e_i) is a finite C-linearly independent family, b is a nonzero complex scalar and L is the internal sum of R(b e_i), then (b e_i) is an R-basis of L. If mu:T->V is R-linear, injective and has image L, the unique preimages of this family form an R-basis of T.

grounds.reason: R is viewed as a subring of C.
The e_i form a complex basis.
mu is injective.
mu is R-linear with the stated image notation.
The image of mu is the internal sum of J e_i.
F003 gives b nonzero and J=Rb.

R004.justification: In a finite relation sum_i r_i b e_i=0, complex independence gives r_i b=0 for every i. Since b is nonzero, every r_i=0 in C and hence in R. The displayed sum supplies spanning. Each vector in this basis lies in the image of mu, so has a unique preimage. Applying mu proves independence of the preimages; expressing mu(t) in the image basis and using injectivity proves their spanning.

R005.fact: For modules over a commutative ring, an additive balanced map on pairs determines a unique linear map out of their tensor product. Pure tensors generate additively, so two linear maps agreeing on all pure tensors agree everywhere; inverse compositions checked on pure tensors give inverse linear maps.

grounds.reason: M_R=R⊗_Z M is the stated module tensor product.
V_K=M⊗_Z K is the stated scalar extension.
S001 constructs ρ and explicitly gives balanced maps and inverse formulas; p acts as zero on K.

R005.justification: The tensor product is the quotient of the free additive group on pairs by additivity and balancing relations. A map respecting those relations descends uniquely, and the classes of the generators span the quotient. This justifies the displayed maps and equality tests without any flatness assumption.

R005.fact: For R commutative and K an R-algebra, c⊗u↦u⊗c gives a K-linear isomorphism K⊗_R U→U⊗_R K, where K acts on the K factor. A linear isomorphism sends a basis to a basis.

grounds.reason: ρ defines the R-algebra structure on K and Φ is proved to be a K-linear isomorphism.
M001 supplies the K-basis 1⊗m_i in K⊗_R M_R.
U=M_R and m_i are supplied by N004 and μ-injectivity; S002 states the switch and its inverse.

R005.justification: Additivity and the relation (ρ(r)c)⊗u=c⊗ru make both switch formulas balanced. Their composites fix pure tensors, hence are identities. Under an invertible linear map, finite spanning expansions transfer, and applying the inverse to any zero linear combination proves independence.

R005.fact: If f is an R-linear endomorphism of U, scalar extension acts by f_K(u⊗c)=f(u)⊗c. Scalar extension preserves identities, sums, compositions, integer powers and scalar multiplication via ρ. Thus a matrix (a_ij) on an R-basis becomes (ρ(a_ij)) on its extended basis; if a is a unit then ρ(a^{-1}) is the inverse of ρ(a).

grounds.reason: N002 supplies preservation of the localized lattice, the matrix-unit operator equality and unit binomial coefficients, as well as the actions of x,y,h.
S002 constructs the compatible extended basis and identifies the lattice operators through μ.
X_r=x^r/r! supplies the complex divided-power equality.
Y_r=y^r/r! supplies the analogous equality.
0≤λ

R005.justification: R-linearity makes f_K balanced. Checking the asserted operations on u⊗c proves them everywhere by generation. Extending a basis expansion applies ρ to its coefficients. The identity aa^{-1}=1 remains an identity under a ring homomorphism. Finally r! is a finite product of nonzero factors in the field K (the empty product is 1), so the extended factorial identities can be divided by r! exactly in the stated range.

R006.fact: For a finite K-basis (β_i) indexed by I, dim_K V_K=|I| and each vector has a unique expansion ∑_{i∈I}c_iβ_i. If |I|>0 then V_K≠0. If a K-subspace W≠{0}, it contains a nonzero vector whose basis expansion has at least one nonzero coefficient.

grounds.reason: N005 gives a K-basis indexed by the finite I of cardinality n>0.
L2 is precisely W≠{0}, with W a K-linear subspace.

R006.justification: Spanning gives a finite expansion and linear independence gives uniqueness. A nonempty independent family contains a nonzero vector, and the finite basis cardinality is its dimension. A subspace contains zero, so inequality with {0} supplies a nonzero member. An expansion with all coefficients zero is zero, hence a nonzero member has a nonzero coefficient.

R006.fact: For L_K=(Zx+Zy+Zh)⊗_Z K with the specified K-linear action, x,y,h span L_K over K. A K-linear subspace of V_K is invariant under L_K if and only if it is invariant under those three operators.

grounds.reason: D016 defines L_K as this tensor product and specifies its induced action and generator tensors.
N005 supplies the induced operators on V_K.
F003 gives the subspace assertion for invariance under all three operators.

R006.justification: Elements of a tensor product are finite sums of pure tensors. Write each first factor as ax+by+ch with integers a,b,c; tensor bilinearity expresses each pure tensor as a K-linear combination of x⊗1,y⊗1,h⊗1. Invariance under the generators therefore implies invariance under each Lie algebra element by linearity of the action and subspace closure. The converse follows by taking each generator.

R001.text: H001 gives n=λ+1>0 and I has n elements. We first prove the commutator formulas for all nonnegative powers. For h, the case t=0 is hv=λv from H003. In the induction step temporarily assume L1: hy^t v=(λ−2t)y^t v. Using [h,y]=−2y from H002, h y^{t+1}v=y h y^t v−2y^{t+1}v=(λ−2(t+1))y^{t+1}v. This proves the step and discharges L1; natural induction proves the h formula for every t≥0. For x, the base t=1 is xyv=yxv+hv=λv by H002 and H003. For t≥1 temporarily assume L2: xy^t v=t(λ−t+1)y^{t−1}v. Then xy^{t+1}v=yxy^t v+hy^t v=[t(λ−t+1)+(λ−2t)]y^t v=(t+1)(λ−t)y^t v. Discharging L2 proves the step, and induction gives the x formula for all t≥1. These identities are F001.

For i∈I, iterating F001 gives x^i y^i v=i! λ(λ−1)⋯(λ−i+1)v. For i=0 the product is 1 and this is v. All factors for i>0 are positive integers, and v≠0 by H003, so every e_i is nonzero over C. By F001, he_i=(λ−2i)e_i; these eigenvalues are distinct over C. To check independence, fix arbitrary coefficients c=(c_i)_{i∈I} and temporarily assume L3: ∑_{i∈I}c_i e_i=0. For each j∈I, apply ∏_{k∈I,k≠j}(h−(λ−2k)Id) to this relation. It yields c_j∏_{k∈I,k≠j}2(k−j)e_j=0. The product, including an empty product, is nonzero, and e_j≠0, hence c_j=0. Discharge L3 to obtain independence. H002 gives dim_C V=n, and there are n independent e_i, so they form a complex basis. This proves F002.

F001 specialized to exponent λ+1 shows that y^{λ+1}v has h-eigenvalue −λ−2 if it is nonzero. Temporarily assume L4 that it is nonzero. Expanding it in the basis F002, the equality h y^{λ+1}v=(−λ−2)y^{λ+1}v forces every coefficient to vanish: for i∈I, (λ−2i)−(−λ−2)=2(λ+1−i) is a nonzero complex scalar. This is a contradiction, so discharge L4 to conclude y^{λ+1}v=0. Applying further y powers gives all higher vanishing. F001 divided by i!, together with this termination and xv=0 from H003, gives xe_0=0, xe_i=(λ−i+1)e_{i−1} for i≥1, ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1} for i<λ, ye_λ=0 and he_i=(λ−2i)e_i. This proves F003.

Iterate the displayed x,y matrices in F003 and divide by r!. For each natural r and i∈I with r≤i, x^r e_i/r!=[(λ−i+1)⋯(λ−i+r)/r!]e_{i−r}=binom(λ−i+r,r)e_{i−r}. If r>i the string reaches e_0 and is killed by x. For i+r≤λ, y^r e_i/r!=[(i+1)⋯(i+r)/r!]e_{i+r}=binom(i+r,r)e_{i+r}; otherwise it passes the last vector and is zero. For r=0 the empty products are 1. These are precisely X_r,Y_r by definition. The displayed binomial coefficients, with nonnegative integer upper argument at least r, are integers. Together with F001–F003 this is every assertion of the asserted conclusion.

R002.text: H004 gives an integer basis of M which is also a complex basis of V. By N001, dim_C V=n and |I|=n. Equality of the cardinalities of finite bases permits reindexing the given lattice basis by I. Thus there exists a family m=(m_i)_{i∈I} which is simultaneously a Z-basis of M and a complex basis of V. This is F001.

Choose such a family m using F001. Since R is a commutative Z-algebra, M001 with A=Z, B=M, C0=R and d=m gives the R-basis (1⊗m_i)_{i∈I} of M_R. Its image under μ is the family m_i in V. A relation in its kernel is a finite R-linear relation among the complex-independent m_i, so all coefficients are zero. Thus μ is injective; the image is free of rank n and spans V over C. By H004, all X_r,Y_r preserve M, so their scalar extensions preserve M_R and μ intertwines them. Also x=X_1 and y=Y_1 preserve M, and h=xy−yx preserves M because H002 gives [x,y]=h. This proves h-stability. Record F002: μ is injective with the claimed free, spanning and stability properties.

For arbitrary i,j∈I evaluate the following operators on the basis from N001. X_λ kills every e_k with k<λ and sends e_λ to e_0 with coefficient 1; Y_λe_0=e_λ, so P0=Y_λX_λ=E_{λλ}. Moreover X_{λ−i}e_λ=e_i with coefficient binom(λ−i,λ−i)=1, giving X_{λ−i}P0=E_{iλ}. For P0Y_{λ−j}, a basis input e_k with k<j is sent below e_λ and killed by P0, one with k>j passes the lowering endpoint and is zero, and e_j is sent to binom(λ,j)e_λ. Hence P0Y_{λ−j}=binom(λ,j)E_{λj}. H001 gives λ<p. No factor of λ!, j!, or (λ−j)! is divisible by p; the factorial identity λ!=binom(λ,j)j!(λ−j)! and primality of p show p does not divide binom(λ,j). Its reciprocal is therefore in R, so it is a unit. Composing the previous identities yields E_ij=binom(λ,j)^{-1}X_{λ−i}P0Y_{λ−j}. F002 supplies preservation by all factors and by R-scalars, proving every E_ij preserves μ(M_R). The proof uses no distinctness of weights in characteristic p, and includes λ=0.

R003.text: Use N002's injective identification M_R⊂V throughout this paragraph. For each i∈I the projection E_ii maps μ(M_R) onto J_i e_i: membership in its image is exactly the definition of J_i. For arbitrary i,j∈I, applying E_ij to c e_j for c∈J_j gives c e_i∈μ(M_R), so J_j⊆J_i; swapping the indices gives equality, including J=J_0 since 0∈I by H001. Each J_i is finitely generated over R: apply its coordinate projection to a finite R-basis of M_R from N002, and take the finitely many resulting complex coefficients as generators. Temporarily assume L1: J=0. Then all J_i are zero, all projections of μ(M_R) vanish, and μ(M_R)=0, contradicting its complex span V and N001's positive dimension. Discharge L1 to obtain J≠0. Finally every vector of μ(M_R) is the sum of its coordinate projections; conversely each J e_i lies in μ(M_R), and N001 gives independence of the e_i. Hence μ(M_R)=⊕_{i∈I}J e_i. This proves F001.

Define S_R=R\{0}, a multiplicative submonoid, and f:J→QJ as the inclusion. Q is a localization of R at S_R: R⊂Q is a domain inclusion, every nonzero element becomes a unit, and every rational a/b is a fraction of elements a,b∈Z⊂R with b≠0. The usual fraction rule for a map inverting S_R is forced and is well-defined by cross multiplication, which is the localization universal property. QJ is a Q-vector space, an R-module by restriction, and these structures form a scalar tower. Since J is finitely generated by F001, its finite generators also span QJ over Q, so QJ is finite-dimensional. Multiplication by any s∈S_R on QJ has inverse multiplication by 1/s. Given z∈QJ, express it as a finite rational combination of elements of J and clear a common nonzero integer denominator s; then s∈S_R and s z=f(c) for some c∈J. Finally equality f(c)=f(c') is equality inside C, so c=c', and the equality condition for localization holds with multiplier 1. These verify all three clauses of IsLocalizedModule(S_R,f), recorded in F002.

Apply M002 with A=R, S=S_R, C0=Q, B=J, B1=QJ, and f the inclusion. F002 gives the localization predicate and all structural conditions. The resulting base-change predicate states exactly that multiplication Q⊗_R J→QJ, q⊗c↦qc, is a Q-linear isomorphism. Thus its map into C is injective, not just an abstract rank calculation. In fraction language a zero image forces a zero numerator, since J⊂C is torsion-free. Define T_Q=Q⊗_R J and r=dim_Q T_Q. The isomorphism and F002 show this dimension is finite. Record F003.

Set A_Q=Q⊗_R M_R. Instantiate the coordinate and insertion maps of F001, denoting them α_i and τ_i. Their scalar extensions give a Q-linear map A_Q→(T_Q)^I sending q⊗u to (q⊗α_i(u))_{i∈I}. Its inverse sends a tuple (z_i) to ∑_{i∈I}(1⊗τ_i)(z_i); here 1⊗τ_i denotes the tensor map q⊗c↦q⊗τ_i(c). These maps are well-defined by R-balancing. The equalities α_iτ_j=δ_ij Id and ∑τ_iα_i=Id in F001 verify the two composite identities, first on pure tensors and then on their finite sums. Thus A_Q≅(T_Q)^I as Q-vector spaces. This proves F004.

N002 supplies an R-basis of M_R with n elements. Apply M001 with A=R, B=M_R and C0=Q to this basis: its scalar extension is a Q-basis of A_Q with n elements, so dim_Q A_Q=n. Apply M003 with A=Q, index type I and constant module family T_Q. The field Q satisfies the strong rank condition by finite-dimensional linear algebra; I is finite with n elements by N001. By F003 each T_Q is finite-dimensional, hence free and finitely generated over Q. M003 gives dim_Q((T_Q)^I)=∑_{i∈I}r=nr. F004 therefore gives n=nr. Since n>0 by N001, cancellation in the natural numbers yields r=1. F003 now gives dim_Q QJ=1, while F001 gives the finite generation, nonzero property and decomposition. This proves all of the asserted conclusion.

R004.text: Choose 0≠a∈J using N003. N003 identifies Q⊗_R J with the one-dimensional subspace QJ⊂C. Since a≠0, a is a Q-basis of that line. Take finite generators of J, discard any zero generators, and use J≠0 to see the remaining list is nonempty. Every remaining generator is a nonzero rational multiple of a. Therefore there exist k≥1 and q_1,…,q_k∈Q\{0} such that J is generated over R by q_1a,…,q_ka. This is F001.

Choose k,q as in F001. For each 1≤j≤k, write q_j as a ratio of nonzero integers, remove the maximal powers of the prime p from numerator and denominator, and define ν_j to be the difference of these two exponents. Then q_j=p^{ν_j}u_j with ν_j∈Z and u_j a rational whose numerator and denominator are both prime to p. Such u_j and its reciprocal belong to R, so u_j is a unit. This construction also covers negative ν_j. Define ν=min_{1≤j≤k}ν_j and b=p^ν a. The minimum exists and is attained because k≥1 and the list is finite. All q_j a belong to Rb, since q_j a=p^{ν_j−ν}u_j b and ν_j−ν≥0. Also b≠0, since p is prime by H001 and a≠0. Record F002, including the existence of a minimizing index.

Choose a minimizing index j0 from F002. Then q_{j0}a=u_{j0}b, and u_{j0} is an R-unit. Since q_{j0}a is a generator of J by F001, b=u_{j0}^{−1}q_{j0}a belongs to J and Rb⊆J. The reverse inclusion follows from F001 and the inclusion of every generator in Rb from F002. Thus J=Rb with b∈J nonzero. This is F003.

Substitute F003 in the direct decomposition of N003 to obtain μ(M_R)=⊕_{i∈I}R(b e_i). The vectors b e_i are R-linearly independent because b≠0 and the e_i are complex-independent by N001. They span by the displayed decomposition, so are an R-basis. Since μ is injective by N002, their unique preimages form an R-basis of M_R. Existentially quantify b to prove the asserted conclusion. In particular no rank-one claim has been inferred from containment in C alone.

R005.text: H001 implies that every integer denominator prime to p maps to a nonzero element of K. Define ρ:R→K by ρ(a/b)=a_K b_K^{−1}. Cross multiplication makes this well-defined and a ring homomorphism extending Z→K. There is also the injective prime-field map F_p→K. Define Φ:M⊗_Z K→M_R⊗_R K by Φ(m⊗c)=(1⊗m)⊗c; its inverse is (r⊗m)⊗c↦m⊗ρ(r)c. Both formulas respect the tensor relations (the R-action on K is through ρ), and the composites are identity on pure tensors, hence on all elements. Next define the map M_R⊗_R K→(M_R/pM_R)⊗_{F_p}K by u⊗c↦(u mod pM_R)⊗c. Its inverse sends a residue tensor (u mod pM_R)⊗c to u⊗c: replacing u by u+pt changes this by pt⊗c=t⊗pc=0. It is balanced over F_p, and its R-balancing is justified by R/pR≅F_p, explicitly a/b mod p↦a_p b_p^{-1}; the kernel is pR and every residue is obtained from an integer. These maps are inverse on generators. All maps commute with operators induced from M or M_R, by their formulas. Such x,y,h and divided powers exist by N002. This proves the natural identifications in F001.

Choose b as in N004. For each i∈I define m_i to be the unique μ-preimage of b e_i; N002 gives injectivity and N004 gives membership and the R-basis property of this family in M_R. Define β_i=Φ^{-1}(m_i⊗1)∈V_K. Apply M001 with A=R, B=M_R, C0=K, the algebra structure ρ and the R-basis (m_i). It gives the K-basis (1⊗m_i) of K⊗_R M_R. The factor-switching isomorphism c⊗u↦u⊗c (with inverse u⊗c↦c⊗u), followed by Φ^{-1}, gives the K-basis β. It has |I|=n=λ+1>0 elements by N001. Because μ intertwines the divided powers, and b is a common complex scalar, the matrices on m_i are exactly those on e_i from N001. F001 carries these matrices to V_K with every integer entry mapped into K. Thus xβ_0=0, xβ_i=(λ−i+1)β_{i−1} for i≥1, yβ_i=(i+1)β_{i+1} for i<λ, yβ_λ=0, and hβ_i=(λ−2i)β_i. The divided-power matrices also descend: X_r^K β_i=binom(λ−i+r,r)β_{i−r} for r≤i, zero for r>i, and Y_r^K β_i=binom(i+r,r)β_{i+r} for i+r≤λ, zero otherwise. Here X_r^K,Y_r^K denote the operators induced from X_r,Y_r on M_R. Record F002.

N002 gives, inside the localized lattice, E_ij=binom(λ,j)^{-1}X_{λ−i}P0Y_{λ−j}, with P0=Y_λX_λ, and says all these factors preserve it. In the basis (b e_i), E_ij has a single entry 1 in position (i,j), the same as in (e_i). Scalar extension through F001 therefore carries the equality to the operator T_ij=ρ(binom(λ,j)^{-1})X_{λ−i}^K P_K Y_{λ−j}^K on β, where P_K=Y_λ^K X_λ^K. It satisfies T_ijβ_k=β_i for k=j and 0 for k≠j. Since binom(λ,j) is a unit of R by N002, its image is a unit of K (ρ sends its inverse to an inverse). Also for 0≤r≤λ<p, no factor of r! is divisible by p by H001, so r! maps to a nonzero element of K. The equalities r!X_r=x^r and r!Y_r=y^r hold over C by definition, hence on M_R by injectivity of μ, and after scalar extension. Consequently X_r^K=(r!)^{-1}x^r and Y_r^K=(r!)^{-1}y^r in this range. This proves F003.

Fix any K-linear subspace W⊂V_K and temporarily assume L1 that W is invariant under x and y. Induction on the power shows it is invariant under x^r and y^r for every natural r. Because W is K-linear it is stable under scalar multiples and compositions of its preserving operators. F003 expresses all X_r^K,Y_r^K for r≤λ as scalar multiples of these powers, and T_ij as a scalar times a composition of these operators, since λ−i,λ,λ−j are all in [0,λ]. Therefore W is invariant under every T_ij. Discharge L1 and universally quantify W. Together with F001–F003, existentially quantify the compatible basis β to obtain the asserted conclusion.

R006.text: Choose a basis β and the compatible matrix operators guaranteed by N005. This basis has n=λ+1>0 elements, so dim_K V_K=n>0 and V_K≠0; record this as F001. Fix an arbitrary K-linear subspace W⊂V_K and temporarily assume L1 that W is invariant under x,y,h. In particular it is x,y-invariant, and N005 says it is invariant under every T_ij. By classical cases, either W={0}, which is already one required alternative, or temporarily assume L2: W≠{0}. Under L1,L2, a nonzero vector in W has a unique expansion in the basis β; at least one coefficient is nonzero, since a vector with every coefficient zero is zero. Thus there exist w∈W, a coefficient family c:I→K, and j∈I with w=∑_{i∈I}c_i β_i≠0 and c_j≠0. This is F002 under L1,L2.

Choose w,c,j as in F002. For every i∈I, linearity and the matrix-unit action in N005 give T_ij w=c_jβ_i∈W. Since c_j≠0 in the field K, multiply by c_j^{-1} to get β_i∈W. All basis vectors belong to W, so W=V_K. Discharge L2 and combine this result with the W={0} case to obtain W={0} or W=V_K under L1. Discharge L1 to get the implication for this arbitrary W, then universally quantify W. This gives F003 with no remaining local assumptions.

F001 proves nonzero dimension and F003 proves exactly the required subspace assertion. L_K is spanned over K by the three induced generators x,y,h, so a K-linear subspace is L_K-invariant exactly when it is invariant under those three operators. Thus these assertions are irreducibility of V(K) as an L(K)-module. The original H001 allows λ=0: then I={0}, every relevant factorial and binomial coefficient is 1, and N005 gives the same one-dimensional conclusion. If p=2 the allowed λ are 0 and 1; N005's matrix-unit argument still applies, with no use of distinct h-eigenvalues in K. Nothing used algebraic closure of K. This proves all of the asserted conclusion.
